_comment: TEMPLATE for OPA gateway authorization data (package gateway.authz, see policies/gateway/authz.rego). Copy this file per environment — e.g. data.staging.json, data.prod.json — fill in real team_id/key_id values, then load it into the ConfigMap key 'gateway' per README.md. Only fields actually read by authz.rego are included below; nothing here is decorative.

config._comment: Fail-open while onboarding a new environment. Flip both to false once every team and key below is registered — see README 'Configuration Flags'.

EXAMPLE_key_id_allowlist_agent.name: EXAMPLE_readonly_agent
EXAMPLE_key_id_allowlist_agent.description: TEMPLATE — allow-list style. Object key must be the real LiteLLM key_id (GET /key/info, token_id column — never the raw sk-... secret).

EXAMPLE_key_id_denylist_agent.name: EXAMPLE_broad_agent
EXAMPLE_key_id_denylist_agent.description: TEMPLATE — deny-list style: no allowed_tools means all tools pass except restricted_tools. Use for agents that need broad access minus specific dangerous actions.

EXAMPLE_key_id_glob_agent.name: EXAMPLE_glob_agent
EXAMPLE_key_id_glob_agent.description: TEMPLATE — glob-style tool lists: allowed_tool_calls / restricted_tool_calls use glob matching (trailing * = case-insensitive prefix, otherwise case-insensitive substring) and may coexist with the exact-match allowed_tools / restricted_tools family; restricted always wins over allowed. allowed_models gates the llm stage alongside the team's list.

EXAMPLE_key_id_tool_argument_constraints.name: EXAMPLE_constrained_tool_agent
EXAMPLE_key_id_tool_argument_constraints.description: TEMPLATE — demonstrates all 4 tool_argument_constraints forms (checked post-call, against the tool_calls the model actually invoked — see README 'Tool call argument constraints'). Copy whichever form(s) you need for your real tool's arguments and delete the rest; any argument NOT listed here is left completely unconstrained (e.g. a free-text 'description' field is usually just omitted).
